themes_detail.label: Waste Collection Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Missed trash collection complaints spiked to 44 this week—329% above the 8-week average of 10.2 per week—signaling a potential sanitation service breakdown in Greenpoint/Williamsburg this week.
evidence: 44 missed collection complaints filed this week vs. 10.2-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 4.95)
329% spike represents largest proportional increase among all monitored complaint categories
Acute timing suggests operational failure rather than seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Interview residents on accumulating trash; check if specific neighborhoods or collection routes are affected
Contact Sanitation Department to determine cause: staffing shortage, route reassignment, equipment failure, or labor action
Cross-reference with CB budget requests for DEP capital spending to assess chronic underfunding

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints from Houses of Worship Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship surged to 3 last week—a 2,300% spike above the 8-week average of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69)—indicating a sudden localized conflict or event this week.
evidence: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical severity)
Baseline of near-zero suggests either new worship activity or new residential sensitivity—acute change either way
Highest z-score among all spikes indicates most anomalous behavior
reporting_angles: Identify which houses of worship are generating complaints; determine if new events, expanded hours, or amplified services started recently
Interview affected residents in adjacent buildings to understand the nature and timing of noise disturbance
Check if this correlates with any recent community board complaints or religious calendar events

themes_detail.label: Police Non-Emergency Calls Surge 271%
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints jumped to 19 this week—a 271% spike above the 5.1-complaint weekly average—suggesting heightened neighborhood safety concerns or increased police visibility this week.
evidence: 19 complaints this week vs. 5.1-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 4.73, severity: high)
271% increase represents sharp uptick in residents calling police for non-emergency issues
Spike could reflect either new crime/disorder or new police enforcement activity drawing complaints
reporting_angles: Analyze NYPD incident reports and arrest data for Greenpoint/Williamsburg to determine if actual crime increased or if enforcement changed
Interview residents and local business owners about perceived safety changes this week
Check NYPD community board meeting minutes or precinct reports for any announced enforcement initiatives

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge 900%
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 5 last week—a 900% spike above the 0.5-complaint weekly average (z-score: 6.36)—suggesting potential violations, expansion, or new resident opposition to street seating this week.
evidence: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.5-complaint baseline (z-score: 6.36, severity: high)
900% increase represents emergence of previously non-contentious issue
Timing suggests either new outdoor seating installations or changed enforcement focus this week
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants or commercial blocks are generating complaints; determine if new outdoor seating was recently installed
Interview community members about what specific violations are being reported: noise, obstruction, capacity, hours
Cross-reference with DOB permits filed in last 90 days to identify new outdoor seating approvals (206 new buildings, 150 ALT-CO filings)

themes_detail.label: Building Violations/Real Estate Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Real Time Enforcement complaints jumped to 17 three weeks ago—a 289% spike above the 4.4-complaint weekly average—combined with IAD (Investigations and Discipline) complaints at 4 three weeks ago (1500% above baseline), suggesting concentrated DOB enforcement activity or developer non-compliance issues.
evidence: Real Time Enforcement complaints: 17 (3 weeks ago) vs. 4.4 baseline (z-score: 4.33)
IAD complaints: 4 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.2 baseline (z-score: 5.67)—combined signal of enforcement or disciplinary action
DOB permits filed in last 90 days: 1,287 total (746 alterations, 206 new buildings)—high development activity may be triggering compliance complaints
reporting_angles: Request DOB records on enforcement actions, violations, and closed cases in Greenpoint/Williamsburg from past 3 weeks; identify pattern
Investigate whether specific development projects (200 Kent Avenue, 20 Berry Street ULURPs in review) are driving complaints
Interview residents about construction complaints, permit violations, or safety concerns tied to recent building activity
